name: 420Explorer
purpose: Canonical-state observability, transaction and contract discovery, protocol decoding, verification metadata and network transparency for 420 Integrated.
invariants: EXP-INV-001: 420Explorer owns no canonical protocol state and requires no Explorer-specific Genesis contract.
EXP-INV-002: Explorer records are projections of chain, consensus and registered protocol state; conflicts resolve in favor of canonical chain data.
EXP-INV-003: Head, safe and finalized states are displayed distinctly and are never collapsed into one confirmation status.
EXP-INV-004: Reorg repair may rewrite only non-finalized indexed history; finalized history is immutable absent an explicit chain-level finality failure procedure.
EXP-INV-005: The complete Explorer index can be rebuilt from supported nodes/RPC, receipts, logs, consensus metadata and registry reads without trusting the hosted Explorer database.
EXP-INV-006: Contract decoding uses runtime bytecode and versioned 420Registry commitments; labels and verified-source metadata cannot change execution truth.
EXP-INV-007: 420 Names and 420 Identity labels are display enrichments only and never replace the underlying address or canonical identity record.
EXP-INV-008: Explorer failure or unavailability cannot prevent direct wallet, RPC, contract or protocol interaction.
EXP-INV-009: Explorer operators gain no custody, smart-account execution, governance, bridge, validator or token-transfer authority.
EXP-INV-010: Public APIs/indexers are replaceable and must expose chain identifiers and indexed/finalized heights so clients can detect stale or wrong-network data.
EXP-INV-011: Transaction, receipt, event and balance presentation must remain traceable to canonical block hashes and chain ID.
EXP-INV-012: Privacy-sensitive off-chain payloads are not made canonical merely because a hash, commitment or transaction reference is visible in Explorer.
